ei.title: Talk It Out, Help Is Here

fullPassage:
Talk It Out, Help Is Here

Host: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program?

Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring psychiatry into the community.

Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could you explain to us how the Friendship Bench program works?

Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.

Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program?

Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.

Host: That's interesting! What happens after patients complete their sessions with the grandmothers?

Dr. Chibanda: When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.

Host: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. And the program has been incredibly successful, right?

Dr. Chibanda: That's correct. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen. We've also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us reach even more people.

Host: That's really amazing! Thank you for your time, Dr. Chibanda. Now let's hear from one of the grandmothers who volunteer for the program. Can you introduce yourself and tell us how you got involved with the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. I knew that I could help heal their wounded hearts by supporting them.

Host: That's very kind of you. Can you tell us about your experience as a grandmother for the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: It's been wonderful. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I've seen how it can make a difference in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.

Host: Thanks for sharing your experiences with us today, Grandma Moyo. It's truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had. And it's all thanks to the hard work of people like you and Dr. Chibanda.

questions.passage: The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients ①<u>had become</u> severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was ②<u>enable</u> to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I ③<u>had never considered</u> such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe ④<u>to pay</u> for transportation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 버스비를 감당할 수 없어서 도움을 받을 수 없었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①had become: 과거완료로 과거 시점 이전의 상태 변화 표현. 정상. ❌ ②enable: 원문은 unable. '~할 수 없는'. enable(가능하게 하다)은 동사이므로 'was enable'은 비문. ✅ ③had never considered: 과거완료로 정상. ✅ ④to pay: 가주어 it, 진주어 to pay 구문으로 정상.
det.tip: unable(형용사: ~할 수 없는) vs enable(동사: ~을 가능하게 하다). be unable to V = cannot V.

questions.passage: These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, ①<u>listening</u> to their stories, and provide them with emotional support. Grandmothers were chosen because they are deeply ②<u>connected</u> to the community. They have all the qualities of a counselor, ③<u>such as</u> excellent listening skills. They are also very reliable, ④<u>which</u> is important for our efforts to support mental health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이야기를 듣고, 정서적 지원을 제공한다.
det.analysis: ❌ ①listening: 원문은 listen. 'volunteer to sit ~, listen ~, and provide ~'에서 sit, listen, provide가 병렬 구조(to에 연결된 동사원형 3개). listening(현재분사)은 병렬 구조 파괴. ✅ ②connected: 'are connected to'에서 수동태/형용사로 정상. ✅ ③such as: '예를 들어'의 전치사구로 정상. ✅ ④which: 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 관계대명사로 정상.
det.tip: 병렬 구조: A, B, and C에서 모든 요소의 형태가 같아야 함. to sit, listen, and provide(모두 동사원형).

questions.passage: I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community ①<u>struggle</u> with mental health problems. I knew that I could help ②<u>heal</u> their wounded hearts by ③<u>supporting</u> them. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing ④<u>to ashame</u> of.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 정신 건강 문제에 대한 도움을 구하는 것은 부끄러워할 일이 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①struggle: 현재시제로 일반적 사실 표현. 정상. ✅ ②heal: 'help heal'에서 help + 동사원형 구문으로 정상. ✅ ③supporting: 전치사 by 뒤 동명사로 정상. ❌ ④to ashame: 원문은 'nothing to be ashamed of'. ashamed는 형용사이므로 be동사가 필요. ashame이라는 동사 형태는 쓰이지 않음.
det.tip: be ashamed of: ~을 부끄러워하다. ashamed는 형용사로 반드시 be동사와 함께 씀. nothing to be ashamed of(부끄러워할 것이 없다).

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide ①<u>accessible</u> mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are ②<u>costly</u> and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with ③<u>emotional</u> support. Grandmothers have the ability to engage in ④<u>meaningful</u> discussions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그 세션은 무료(free)이며 존경받는 노인 여성들에 의해 제공된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①accessible: '접근 가능한' → 적절. ❌ ②costly: '비용이 많이 드는'. 원문은 free(무료의). 무료 세션인데 costly(비싼)로 바꾸면 문맥 반대. ✅ ③emotional: '정서적' 지원 → 적절. ✅ ④meaningful: '의미 있는' 토론 → 적절.
det.tip: free(무료의) ↔ costly(비용이 많이 드는). 접근성 높은 프로그램의 핵심 특징이 무료 제공.

questions.passage: In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are ①<u>available</u> in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking ②<u>distance</u>. We've also started ③<u>reducing</u> the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us ④<u>reach</u> even more people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 저희는 또한 프로그램을 확장(expanding)하기 시작했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①available: '이용 가능한' → 적절. ✅ ②distance: 'walking distance(도보 거리)' → 적절. ❌ ③reducing: '축소하는'. 원문은 expanding(확장하는). 온라인 상담까지 제공하는 맥락에서 reducing은 정반대. ✅ ④reach: '다가가다' → 적절.
det.tip: expanding(확장하다) ↔ reducing(축소하다). 프로그램이 성장하고 온라인까지 확장하는 맥락.

questions.passage: Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program? The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. I needed to find a way to bring __________ into the community.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정신의학을 지역 사회에 도입할 방법을 찾아야 했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① education
✅ ② psychiatry
❌ ③ transportation
❌ ④ entertainment
정신과 의사가 부족한 상황에서 정신의학(psychiatry)을 지역 사회에 도입하려는 맥락. ① education(교육), ③ transportation(교통), ④ entertainment(오락)는 정신과 의사 부족 문제의 해결과 무관.
det.tip: psychiatry(정신의학): 정신 건강 치료를 지역 사회 수준에서 제공하겠다는 Dr. Chibanda의 핵심 구상.

questions.passage: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. This means the grandmothers were selected because they have both __________ and trustworthiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할머니들은 상담 기술과 신뢰성을 모두 갖추고 있어 선정되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① medical expertise
❌ ② financial resources
✅ ③ counseling skills
❌ ④ academic degrees
경청 기술, 공감, 토론 참여 능력은 모두 '상담 기술(counseling skills)'에 해당. trustworthiness는 reliable에서 도출. ① medical expertise(의료 전문성)는 할머니들의 역할과 다름. ② financial resources, ④ academic degrees는 언급 없음.
det.tip: 빈칸추론: 앞에 나열된 구체적 사항(listening skills, empathy, ability to discuss)을 포괄하는 상위 개념을 찾아야 함.

questions.passage: Host: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Dr. Dixon Chibanda는 우정 벤치 프로그램의 창시자이다.
오늘 방송에는 세 명의 특별한 손님이 있다.

det.korean: Dr. Dixon Chibanda는 우정 벤치 프로그램의 창시자(founder)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Dr. Dixon Chibanda는 우정 벤치 프로그램의 창시자이다.
❌ ② 우정 벤치는 남아프리카공화국에 있다.
❌ ③ 오늘 방송에는 세 명의 특별한 손님이 있다.
❌ ④ 우정 벤치는 학교에 설치된 벤치이다.
① 'the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda'와 일치. ② Zimbabwe(짐바브웨)이지 남아공이 아님. ③ two special guests(2명). ④ park benches(공원 벤치)이지 학교가 아님.
det.tip: Zimbabwe(짐바브웨)는 아프리카 남부의 국가. South Africa(남아프리카공화국)와 다른 나라.

questions.passage: That's correct. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 2022년에 약 9만 명의 환자에게 대면 상담을 제공했다.
우정 벤치는 현재 전국 20곳 이상의 지역에서 이용 가능하다.
모두가 걸어서 갈 수 있는 거리에 우정 벤치를 갖는 것이 비전이다.
이미 모든 지역에서 우정 벤치를 이용할 수 있다.

det.korean: 아직 모든 지역이 아니라 20곳 이상이며, '비전'으로 걸어서 갈 수 있는 거리를 목표하고 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 2022년에 약 9만 명의 환자에게 대면 상담을 제공했다.
❌ ② 우정 벤치는 현재 전국 20곳 이상의 지역에서 이용 가능하다.
❌ ③ 모두가 걸어서 갈 수 있는 거리에 우정 벤치를 갖는 것이 비전이다.
✅ ④ 이미 모든 지역에서 우정 벤치를 이용할 수 있다.
④ 원문은 'more than twenty different regions'이고 'Our vision is for everyone to ~'이므로 아직 모든 지역은 아님. ①②③은 원문과 일치.
det.tip: vision(비전): 아직 실현되지 않은 목표. 'we are working hard to make it happen'이 목표 미달성의 근거.

questions.passage: Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it.
questions.stem: Grandma Moyo에 대한 다음 설명 중 옳은 것은?
ch: 지역 사회의 정신 건강 문제에 대해 무언가를 하고 싶어서 합류했다.

det.korean: 지역 사회의 정신 건강 문제에 대해 무언가를 하고 싶어서 프로그램에 합류했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 그녀는 전문 정신과 의사이다.
❌ ② 프로그램에 참여한 지 약 18년이 되었다.
✅ ③ 지역 사회의 정신 건강 문제에 대해 무언가를 하고 싶어서 합류했다.
❌ ④ 그녀는 56세이다.
③ 'I wanted to do something about it'과 일치. ① 정신과 의사가 아닌 자원봉사 할머니. ② about eight years(약 8년)이지 18년이 아님. ④ 76세(I'm 76 years old)이지 56세가 아님.
det.tip: eight(8) ≠ eighteen(18), 76 ≠ 56. 숫자 함정에 주의.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. Grandmothers were chosen because they are deeply connected to the community and have all the qualities of a counselor. When the sessions are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group. In 2022, we provided counseling to about 90,000 patients.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 지역 사회 중심의 정신 건강 치료 프로그램의 운영과 성과

det.korean: 글 전체가 우정 벤치 프로그램의 운영 방식과 성과를 설명하고 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 짐바브웨의 경제적 어려움과 교통 문제
✅ ② 지역 사회 중심의 정신 건강 치료 프로그램의 운영과 성과
❌ ③ 노인 자원봉사자들의 고충과 보상
❌ ④ 온라인 상담 앱의 개발 과정
② 프로그램 운영(할머니 상담사, 커뮤니티 그룹)과 성과(9만 명 상담)를 다루고 있음. ① 경제적 어려움은 배경일 뿐 주제가 아님. ③ 할머니들의 고충은 언급 없음. ④ 앱은 부수적 확장.
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심. 도입부의 배경이나 마지막의 부수적 정보를 주제로 혼동하지 말 것.

questions.passage: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. The program provides accessible mental health services through talk therapy sessions led by community grandmothers. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Friendship Benches: Healing Through Community Conversations
Zimbabwe's Economic Crisis and Mental Health
The Grandmother Revolution: A Political Movement

det.korean: 우정 벤치: 지역 사회 대화를 통한 치유.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Friendship Benches: Healing Through Community Conversations
❌ ② Zimbabwe's Economic Crisis and Mental Health
❌ ③ The Grandmother Revolution: A Political Movement
❌ ④ Modern Medicine Meets Traditional Therapy
① 프로그램의 핵심(대화를 통한 지역 사회 치유)을 정확히 반영. ② 경제 위기는 배경일 뿐. ③ 정치 운동이 아닌 건강 프로그램. ④ 전통 의학과의 연결은 원문에 없음.
det.tip: 제목은 글의 핵심 메시지를 함축적으로 표현. 지나치게 넓거나 좁은 선택지를 제거.

questions.passage: However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years.
questions.stem: Dr. Chibanda가 "This shocked me"라고 말한 것에 함축된 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 경제적 이유로 치료를 받지 못하는 현실을 처음 인식했다.

det.korean: 교통비 때문에 치료를 받지 못하는 현실을 처음 인식했다는 충격.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 환자의 우울증 증상이 예상보다 심각했다.
❌ ② 정신과 의사의 수가 예상보다 적었다.
❌ ③ 버스 요금이 갑자기 인상되었다.
✅ ④ 경제적 이유로 치료를 받지 못하는 현실을 처음 인식했다.
④ 'I had never considered such a problem before(전에 이런 문제를 생각해 본 적 없었다)'가 핵심. 의사로서 환자가 경제적 이유로 치료 접근이 불가능하다는 현실을 처음 깨달은 충격. ① 우울증 심각도가 아닌 접근성 문제. ② 의사 부족은 별개 문장. ③ 요금 인상 언급 없음.
det.tip: 함축의미 추론: 직접 말한 것이 아닌 그 뒤에 숨은 의미를 파악. 'never considered before'가 핵심 단서.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches. They listen to their stories and provide <u>them</u> with emotional support.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할머니들이 환자들에게 정서적 지원을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the grandmothers
✅ ② the patients
❌ ③ the sessions
❌ ④ the benches
them은 'provide them with emotional support'에서 정서적 지원을 받는 대상, 즉 patients. 할머니들이 환자들과 함께 앉아 이야기를 듣고 지원을 제공하는 구조.
det.tip: 지칭추론: 대명사가 가리키는 대상을 문맥에서 파악. 주어(These women) ≠ 목적어(them = patients).

questions.passage: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group. The group is made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. <u>This</u> is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 This가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 환자들이 커뮤니티 지원 그룹에 참여하는 것
그룹 구성원들이 서로 쉽게 공감하고 지지할 수 있는 것

det.korean: 구성원들이 서로 쉽게 공감하고 지지할 수 있는 것의 이유가 뒤에 나온다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 환자들이 커뮤니티 지원 그룹에 참여하는 것
❌ ② 할머니들과의 세션이 끝나는 것
✅ ③ 그룹 구성원들이 서로 쉽게 공감하고 지지할 수 있는 것
❌ ④ 환자들이 비슷한 어려움을 겪는 것
This is because ~에서 This는 바로 앞 문장 'can easily relate to and support one another'를 가리킴. 그 이유가 '같은 커뮤니티 출신 + 비슷한 어려움 경험'이기 때문.
det.tip: 'This is because ~'에서 This는 앞 문장의 내용을 가리키고, because 이하가 그 이유를 설명.

questions.passage: Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe. Host: That's interesting! What happens after patients complete their sessions with the grandmothers? Dr.
questions.stem: 할머니들이 프로그램에 선정된 이유 중 하나로, 상담가로서 갖춘 자질에 해당하는 **영어** 핵심 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: 상담가의 자질: 경청 기술, 공감, 의미 있는 토론 참여 능력.
det.analysis: 원문에서 상담가 자질로 나열된 것 중 empathy(공감)가 1단어 핵심 답변. listening skills(2단어)는 조건 불충족.
det.tip: empathy(공감): 다른 사람의 감정을 이해하고 함께 느끼는 능력. 상담에서 가장 중요한 자질 중 하나.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. These women volunteer to sit with patients at the benches and provide them with emotional support. Grandmothers were chosen because they are deeply connected to the community.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 올바른 형태를 쓰시오.

The Friendship Bench program has been incredibly __________. [success]

det.korean: 우정 벤치 프로그램은 매우 성공적이었다.
det.analysis: be동사(has been) 뒤에 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 필요. success(명사: 성공) → successful(형용사: 성공적인). incredibly가 수식하므로 부사+형용사 구조.
det.tip: success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사). be동사 뒤에는 형용사가 온다.

questions.passage: It's truly inspiring __________________________________________. And it's all thanks to the hard work of people like you and Dr. Chibanda.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.

[ the / that / influence / had / see / program / the / Friendship Bench / has / to ]
questions.wa: to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had
accept: TO SEE THE INFLUENCE THAT THE FRIENDSHIP BENCH PROGRAM HAS HAD
To see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had
to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had
to see the influence that the friendship bench program has had
to see the influence that the friendship bench program has had.

det.korean: 우정 벤치 프로그램이 미친 영향력을 보는 것은 정말 고무적이다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'It's truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had.' 가주어 it + 진주어 to see. 'the influence that ~ has had'에서 that은 관계대명사.
det.tip: it is + 형용사 + to V: 가주어/진주어 구문. the influence that S has had: S가 미친 영향력.

questions.ans: to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had
